chunks: And whatever is in it from Hamzah ibn Himran, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hamzah ibn Himran ibn A'yan, the freed slave of Banu Shayban Al-Kufi.

key_terms.الْكُوفِيِّ: Al-Kufi, indicating his origin from Kufa.
key_terms.حَمَزَةُ بْنُ حُمْرَانَ: Hamzah ibn Himran, a prominent companion of the Imams whose narrations are cited.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect used for the narrator.
key_terms.مَوْلَى بَنِي شَيْبَانَ: The freed slave of Banu Shayban, indicating his social status and tribal affiliation.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, a famous companion of Imam Al-Reza and Imam Al-Jawad.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a key narrator in the chain, often identified as Ibn Abi Zaynab.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ الصَّفَّارِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, a well-known narrator and scholar.
key_terms.يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ: Ya'qub ibn Yazid, a narrator in the chain.

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Hamzah ibn Himran's hadiths in Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous verification of the *isnad* for narrations by Hamzah ibn Himran, a prominent companion of Imam al-Sadiq. By tracing the chain through key figures like Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Ja'far ibn Yunus, al-Saduq underscores the reliability of these reports within the Shia scholarly tradition, emphasizing the importance of continuous, authenticated transmission from the Imams.
